spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The parameter b is doing double duty: its real part supplies vertical oscillation, while its imaginary part shifts Re(s). Complexifying b therefore turns what looks like a critical-line formula into one integral family spanning 0<Re(s)<2; the subsequent change of variables reveals the cleaner kernel 1/y-1/sinh(y).

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Using evenness, the source writes the real-line integral over the positive half-line. It sets b=b'+iq, so s=1/2+ib=(1/2-q)+ib' and -3/2<q<1/2 gives 0<Re(s)<2. Substitution into Eq. (2.6), followed by pi x^2=y, produces Eqs. (2.7)-(2.8) with a y^{-s}(1/y-1/sinh(y)) kernel.
directed.conceptual_reading: The apparent restriction to Re(s)=1/2 is reinterpreted as a parametrization artifact: allowing the auxiliary parameter to be complex moves transversely across a strip without changing the kernel family. The y-variable then packages cancellation at the origin and decay at infinity into a representation suited to further transforms.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is first parametric, b to s, and then analytic, x to y. Together they convert an oscillatory critical-line power into a Mellin-type strip representation with the hyperbolic-sine subtraction as its central kernel.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The claimed strip still excludes the zeta pole: on Re(s)=1 the source requires Im(s) nonzero. The span states the extended validity but does not supply a full analytic-continuation or endpoint-convergence argument, so the open-strip domain should not be enlarged from this evidence.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Expanding sinh(y)-y decomposes the integral kernel into odd monomials, each of which is recognized by a standard 1/sinh(y) moment. The integral representation is thereby converted term by term into Gamma factors times zeta values at shifted arguments.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source rewrites the Eq. (2.8) integrand using (sinh(y)-y)/sinh(y), expands sinh(y)-y as y^3/3!+y^5/5!+..., exchanges the resulting sum with the integral, and applies the moment formula integral_0^infinity y^k/sinh(y) dy=(2-2^{-k})Gamma(1+k)zeta(1+k), stated for k>0. This yields the Gamma-weighted shifted-zeta series in Eq. (3.5).
directed.conceptual_reading: The power-series expansion diagonalizes the complicated kernel into moments that an existing transform evaluates explicitly. It is a basis-change move: local monomials of the hyperbolic numerator become shifted zeta arguments, while factorial coefficients control their assembly.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge chain is hyperbolic subtraction to odd-power series, odd powers to 1/sinh moments, and moments to Gamma times shifted zeta. Eq. (3.2) is the lookup transform that makes the representation change operational.
directed.boundary_or_failure: The span does not justify exchanging the infinite power series with the improper integral or spell out the s-domain ensuring the substituted moment parameter satisfies its hypotheses. The conventional functional equation displayed first is context, not a derivation of Eq. (3.5).
directed.uncertainty: Indices, factorials, exponents, powers of two, and Gamma arguments in Eqs. (3.1)-(3.5) are fragile in the normalized layout. The mechanism is explicit, but formula-exact use and convergence claims require scan and analytic verification.

related_synthesis_entries.title: Kernel engineering to shifted-zeta identity

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The shifted-zeta series is split against the baseline zeta(q)=1+[zeta(q)-1]. The baseline Gamma series is summed in closed form, leaving a residual zeta-minus-one tail; this separates an analytically tractable bulk contribution from the genuinely shifted-zeta remainder.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Starting from Eq. (3.5), the source sums the component obtained by replacing each shifted zeta factor by 1, giving the Gamma expression in Eq. (3.6). It then writes Eq. (3.7) as a series weighted by zeta(2n-s+1)-1 plus that closed contribution, and says the resulting identity appears new.
directed.conceptual_reading: Subtracting the limiting baseline 1 is a decomposition that isolates structure: the easily summable part is absorbed into explicit Gamma terms, while the residual tail records the departure of shifted zeta values from that baseline. This can also improve conceptual control of which part is closed and which remains infinite.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The bridge is an add-and-subtract decomposition inside the Gamma-weighted series. Eq. (3.6) evaluates the zeta-free branch, and recombination produces a closed term plus a shifted zeta-minus-one series in Eq. (3.7).
directed.boundary_or_failure: The packet provides no independent check of the closed summation, the convergence or analytic domain of the decomposed series, or the claimed novelty. The decomposition is not evidence that Eq. (3.7) has better numerical or analytic behavior without further bounds.
directed.uncertainty: Eq. (3.6) and the nested Gamma ratios and parentheses in Eq. (3.7) are visibly extraction-fragile. The baseline-splitting mechanism is clear, but the exact identity and novelty claim remain source assertions pending scan and independent verification.
